The time signals excited at different moments can be separated under the Assumption \ref{sump}.

issues.failure_explanation: From the convolution representation, the pulse at t_j produces far-field signal supported in retarded times t in [t_j - c^{-1} xhat·a(t_j) - c^{-1} sup(xhat·D_j), t_j - c^{-1} xhat·a(t_j) - c^{-1} inf(xhat·D_j)]. Condition (2) bounds only c^{-1}diam(D_{j-1}) and ignores both the trajectory displacement c^{-1}xhat·(a(t_j)-a(t_{j-1})) and the width of D_j. Counterexample: c=1, xhat=e_1, a(t)=(0.9t,0,0), D_j=B_{d/2}, t_j=2dj satisfies (2) (2d>d) and |a'|<c, yet consecutive signals occupy [0.1t_j-d/2, 0.1t_j+d/2], which overlap. So the asserted separability is false.

failure_location.quote: The second assumption ensures that wave signals generated at different instants remain separable due to non-overlapping supports.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace Assumption (2) by a true gap condition obtained from the same convolution formula, e.g. t_j-t_{j-1} > c^{-1}(|a(t_j)-a(t_{j-1})| + (diam D_j + diam D_{j-1})/2) uniformly in the observation directions; then the separation argument and Corollary cor:added-1 hold.
issues.overall_effect: The reduction of (ISP') to per-pulse data (and hence the practical multi-pulse reconstruction pipeline) is not guaranteed for admissible moving sources; measured signals of different instants may overlap and contaminate the u_j^infty used in Corollary cor:added-1.
issues.title: Assumption (2) does not ensure separability of the emitted signals
issues.why_classification: The repair is one corrected, explicitly computable hypothesis; the single-pulse theory and the multi-pulse corollary and all guarantees survive unchanged for every intended application.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem A.1 needs T_# coercive, i.e. |S| bounded below, which Assumption sum (4) does not provide. Take D the unit ball and S(y)=|y-y_0|^3 (or any sign-changing S with a nodal surface, e.g. S(y)=y_1): all of Assumption sum holds but int_D |S|^{-1}dy=infinity, so 1 is not in Range(T^{1/2}). Writing T=UM with U unimodular multiplication and M multiplication by S/sqrt(2pi)>=0 gives F=(L U M^{1/2})(L U M^{1/2})^*, hence by Douglas' lemma Range(F_#^{1/2})=L(Range(M^{1/2})), and since L is injective this is a proper subset of Range(L)=L(L^2(D)) (e.g. L1 lies in Range(L) but not in Range(F_#^{1/2})). The proof's only device for the missing coercivity is the passage to the limit of ranges from norm convergence of F_epsilon to F, which is invalid: Picard weight conditions sum |c_n|^2/lambda_n<infinity are not preserved under norm limits.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restore the strict positivity hypothesis of the cited prior work, e.g. replace Assumption sum (4) by |S(y)| >= c_0 > 0 on the closure of D; then T_# is coercive and Theorem A.1 yields the range identity directly, restoring every dependent claim in that regime.
issues.overall_effect: For every source with zeros the Picard sums characterize Range(F_#^{1/2}) and not Range(L), so the finiteness criterion behind I_eta, W_eta, h, I^(xhat), I and W and all uniqueness statements derived from them is unreliable; the admissible source class must be cut back essentially to the classical one.
issues.title: Range identity Range(F_#^{1/2})=Range(L) fails for sources allowed by Assumption 1
issues.why_classification: The counterexample covers exactly the regime the paper advertises as a main innovation (sources whose nodal set has measure zero), and the identity holds only when |S| is essentially bounded below; every source-supported repair therefore excludes that advertised regime and abandons the stated generality, although a classical-positivity version of the theorem survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \phi^{(\hat{x})}_{z,\eta}(k):= e^{-i k\,  (c^{-1}\hat{x}\cdot z -\eta)}=e^{-i k\,b_{z,\eta}^{(\hat{x})}},\qquad k\in {\mgq (0, K)}.

issues.failure_explanation: Lu and phi_{z,eta} are elements of L^2(0,K). Extended by zero (the only reading compatible with the displayed definition of F^{-1}), their inverse Fourier transforms are band-limited entire functions of t, which have support all of R unless zero (Paley-Wiener), so the claimed compact support is false; the same computation in the proof of Theorem lem3.4 replaces F^{-1} of the truncated exponential e^{-ikb}chi_{(0,K)} by a Dirac mass delta(.-b), whereas it equals (e^{iK(t-b)}-1)/(i sqrt(2pi)(t-b)). The statements hold only after replacing Lu and phi by their entire extensions to all of R (inverse transforms pi_#(u dy) and delta_b), a change of meaning never declared and one that in fact contradicts the 'if' direction of Theorem lem3.4.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Declare that Lu and phi_{z,eta} are taken through their entire extensions to R (equivalently define F^{-1} on that class and read 'support' distributionally); then the lemma and the delta identity hold literally, and the interval endpoints must carry t_0 instead of the free variable t.
issues.overall_effect: The support lemma and the pointwise (Dirac) computation used in the converse part of Theorem lem3.4's proof are meaningless as written; all support-based reasoning needs the objects redefined first.
issues.title: Support lemma and Dirac computation misuse the inverse Fourier transform of band-limited functions
issues.why_classification: A short, local clarification of the domain/extension convention restores the lemma and the proof step it feeds, with no new argument and no change to any otherwise valid claim.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Choose the set $\{y_m\}_{m=1}^{\infty}$ such that $y=y_1$.Then we have $\phi^{(\hat{x})}_{z,\eta} \in $ Range $(L_N)$ for all $N\geq 1$. By Lemma \ref{lem4.1} (ii), it holds that $\phi^{(\hat{x})}_{z,\eta} \in $ Range $(L)$.

issues.failure_explanation: For w in L^2(D) the function tau -> (Lw)(tau)=int_D e^{-i tau b_y} w(y)dy extends to an entire function whose inverse Fourier transform is the pushforward pi_#(w dy), y -> b_y, an absolutely continuous finite measure on R. If (Lw)(tau)=e^{-i tau b} held on (0,K), analyticity would extend it to all tau, forcing pi_#(w dy)=delta_b, impossible for an absolutely continuous measure. Hence phi_{z,eta} is never in Range(L), for any z and eta, and the 'if' direction (and the whole finiteness criterion) is false. The proof illegitimately transfers the discrete conclusion phi in Range(L_N)=span{e^{-i tau a_m}} (where pure exponentials do occur) to the continuum through the undefined and false identity Range(L)=lim_N Range(L_N).

failure_location.quote: For any $\eta \in \R$, there holds $z \in {K}_{D,\eta}^{(\hat{x})}$ if and only if $\phi^{(\hat{x})}_{z,\eta} \in $ Range $(L)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must replace the point test functions (or the source space L^2(D)) by objects for which a genuine range criterion holds and re-derive the factorization, indicator and uniqueness theory from the beginning.
issues.overall_effect: All indicator-based characterizations (W_eta, h, I^(xhat), I, W) and every uniqueness statement derived from them (determination of t_0, of the strip K_D^(xhat), of the Theta-hull, of ch(D), and the multi-pulse corollary) lose their justification; with exact data the Picard sums diverge at every sampling point, so the indicators vanish identically and no imaging criterion is delivered.
issues.title: Pointwise range characterization of Theorem lem3.4 is false (test functions never lie in Range(L))
issues.why_classification: The central range characterization is false at every sampling point, not merely unproven, and the discrete-to-continuous step that purports to prove it is void; no comparable version of the point-test-function criterion follows from the source, so essentially new arguments and a re-derivation of all indicator and uniqueness claims are unavoidable.

issues.failure_explanation: |Re F|+|Im F| is not a spectral function of F: for the Toeplitz matrix of (matF) the matrices F, Re F=(F+F^*)/2 and Im F generically do not commute, hence do not share eigenvectors (e.g. F=[[1,0],[2,1]] gives Re F=[[1,1],[1,1]], which does not commute with F). The stated identity of eigenpairs, and thus the values lambda_n=|Re lambda~_n|+|Im lambda~_n|, hold only in the circulant/commuting case. Followed literally, the discrete Picard sums use the wrong eigenpairs and do not approximate the indicator I_eta^(xhat).

failure_location.quote: then one deduces that  an eigen-system of the matrix $(F^{(\hat x)})_\#:= |\real (F^{(\hat x)})|+|\ima(F^{(\hat x)})|$ is $\left\{ ( \lambda^{(\hat x)}_n, \psi^{(\hat x)}_n): n=1,2,\cdots,N \right\}$, where $ \lambda^{(\hat x)}_n:=|\real (\tilde \lambda^{(\hat x)}_n)| +|\ima (\tilde \lambda^{( \hat x)}_n)|$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Diagonalize the SPD matrix (F^(xhat))_# itself and use its eigenpairs in the Picard sums, as the source itself notes as an alternative.
issues.overall_effect: All numerical indicator values computed from the prescribed eigenpairs, and hence the reconstructions based on them, do not approximate the theoretical indicators; the algorithm as documented computes a different quantity.
issues.title: Discrete recipe claims F_# shares eigenvectors with F and uses the wrong eigenvalues
issues.why_classification: Replacing one eigensolver step by the correct alternative (already indicated in the source) is a purely local change that preserves the entire numerical procedure and all of its intended guarantees.
